tables.label: Table 1
tables.caption: Peptide design and their key physicochemical parameters.
footnotes: Molecular weight (MW) was measured by mass spectroscopy (MS).

tables.label: Table 2
tables.caption: Antimicrobial and hemolytic values of the peptides.
footnotes: Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) were determined as the lowest concentration of the peptides that inhibited bacteria growth. The tests were performed at least three times in duplicate.
P. aeruginosa variant 1 was obtained by step-wise culture with ciprofloxacin hydrochloride.
P. aeruginosa variant 2 was obtained by step-wise culture with gentamicin.
MHC is the minimum concentration that caused 5% hemolysis of human red blood cells (hRBC). When no 5% hemolysis was observed at 256 µM, a value of 512 µM was used to calculate the therapeutic index.
GM denotes the geometric mean of MIC values from all microbial strains in this table.
Therapeutic index (TI) is the ratio of the MHC to the geometric mean of MICs (GM). Larger values indicate greater cell selectivity.

tables.label: Table 3
tables.caption: MIC values of peptides in the presence of physiological saltsa with E. coli ATCC25922 and P. aeruginosa ATCC27853.
footnotes: Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) were determined as the lowest concentration of the peptides that anti-bacteria growth.

The final concentrations of NaCl, KCl, NH4Cl, MgCl2, CaCl2, ZnCl2, and FeCl3 were 150 mM, 4.5 mM, 6 µM, 1 mM, 8 µM, and 4 µM, respectively, and the control MIC values were determined in the absence of these physiological salts.
The medium contained all kinds of salts in physiological concentrations.

tables.label: Table 4
tables.caption: MIC values of peptides R-FV-I16 and ME26 treated with serum, enzymes and heat.
